title: How to Remove Pet Hair From a Couch | Ze Home Finds
h1: how to get pet hair off your couch — for good
description: Simple ways to remove dog and cat hair from couches, beds and clothes, plus how to reduce shedding at the source with a steam pet brush. South African pet owners' guide.
intro: If you share your home with a cat or dog, you share your couch with their fur. Here's a routine that actually keeps on top of it — tackling the fur already on your furniture and cutting down how much ends up there in the first place.

body: Most of the fur on your couch is loose undercoat that would come out with a good brush. A few minutes of brushing a few times a week catches it before it lands on the furniture.
A steam pet brush makes this easier: the fine mist helps lift loose fur and loosen tangles, and many pets tolerate it better than a dry brush.

sections.h2: 2. Use a reusable roller instead of sticky sheets
body: Sticky lint rollers work, but you keep buying refills and binning sheets. A reusable pet hair roller has a fabric surface that grabs hair as you roll it back and forth; you open it and empty the collected fur straight into the bin.
Fur collects in seams and between cushions. A small cordless handheld vacuum gets into those gaps quickly — and it's handy for the car seats your dog loves too.
Put a washable throw where your pet likes to sleep and wash it weekly. It's far easier to shake out a blanket than to de-fur the whole couch.

A healthy coat sheds less. Make sure your dog always has water — especially on walks in the South African heat. A leak-proof water bottle with a built-in bowl makes that easy, and it's included in our Pet Grooming Kit. If shedding seems excessive, check in with your vet.

faqs.q: What removes pet hair from a couch best?
faqs.a: A reusable pet hair roller for the fabric surface plus a handheld vacuum for seams and crevices. Brushing your pet regularly reduces how much fur lands there.

title: Flame Diffuser vs Candles: Which Is Better? | Ze Home Finds
h1: flame diffuser vs candles: which is better?
description: Flame diffuser or scented candles? We compare ambience, safety, running cost and scent so you can choose the right one for your bedroom or lounge in South Africa.
intro: Candles are the classic way to make a room feel cosy. The viral flame diffuser is the newer alternative. Here's how they compare on the things that matter at home.

body: Candles give a real, warm flicker. A flame diffuser imitates it with LED light shining through rising mist — on video and in a dim room it looks remarkably like a real flame, and some diffusers switch between colours.

A candle is an open flame: you can't leave it burning when you leave the room or fall asleep, and it's a risk around kids, pets and curtains. A flame diffuser has no fire and nothing to light, which is why people use it as a night light.
Scented candles release fragrance as the wax burns. A diffuser uses a few drops of essential oil in water, so you can change the scent whenever you like — lavender at night, citrus in the morning.
Candles burn down and need replacing. A diffuser is a once-off purchase; after that you only buy essential oils, and a small bottle lasts a long time at a few drops per use.
Because it's an ultrasonic humidifier, a flame diffuser also adds moisture to dry air — welcome in Highveld winters. Candles don't do that.
Love the ritual of a real flame? Keep a candle for dinner. For everyday ambience, bedtime and anywhere you'd rather not worry, a flame diffuser is the easier choice.

faqs.q: Is a flame diffuser safe to leave on?
faqs.a: There is no real flame — it's mist lit by an LED — so there's nothing to burn. Follow the instructions for water level and keep it on a stable surface.

faqs.q: Can you use any essential oil in a flame diffuser?
faqs.a: Use a few drops of water-soluble essential oil in the water tank.
